title: Queuing and Inventory Models
subject: LIT 803
description: Twenty-five questions across easy, medium and hard on queuing measures and the EOQ model, with short calculations on the desk, nursery and fuel oil examples.

questions.prompt: What two competing costs does queuing theory balance?
options: Customer waiting costs and server service costs
questions.explanation: More servers lower waiting costs but raise service costs.

questions.prompt: What does λ stand for in queuing?
options: The mean service rate per server
The mean arrival rate of customers
questions.explanation: It is measured in customers per unit time.

questions.prompt: What does μ stand for in queuing?
options: The mean service rate per active server
questions.explanation: It is also in customers per unit time.

questions.prompt: How is the utilisation factor ρ defined?
questions.explanation: s is the number of parallel servers.

questions.prompt: What does Lq measure?
options: The average number of customers waiting in line
The average time in the system
The average number in the whole system
questions.explanation: L counts customers waiting and being served.

questions.prompt: What does W measure?
options: The average time in line only
The total average time a customer spends in the system
questions.explanation: Wq is the time in line only.

questions.prompt: What question does the Economic Order Quantity answer?
questions.explanation: The reorder point answers when to order.

questions.prompt: What is carrying (holding) cost?
options: The cost of placing an order
The cost of storing inventory, such as space, insurance, capital tied up and spoilage
The cost of delivery to a customer
questions.explanation: Ordering cost is the fixed cost of each order, and shortage cost arises when stock runs out.

questions.prompt: As more servers are added to a queue, what happens to the two costs?
options: Service cost falls and waiting cost rises
Service cost rises and customer waiting cost falls
questions.explanation: The best service level is where the total of the two is lowest.

questions.prompt: How is the average number in the system related to the average number in the queue?
questions.explanation: λ/μ is the average number being served.

questions.prompt: How is the average waiting time in line found?
questions.explanation: This is the same relationship as W = L / λ for the whole system.

questions.prompt: Which of the EOQ assumptions is correct?
options: Demand is continuous, constant and known, and shortages are not allowed
Orders arrive a few units at a time
questions.explanation: The five assumptions also include constant lead time, instant arrival of a full batch and a fixed unit price.

questions.prompt: How is the annual ordering cost calculated in the EOQ model?
questions.explanation: H/Q is the number of orders per year, and S is the cost of each.

questions.prompt: How is the annual carrying cost calculated?
questions.explanation: Q/2 is the average stock held.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for the optimal order quantity?
questions.explanation: It comes from setting dA/dQ = −HS/Q² + KP/2 equal to zero.

questions.prompt: What is true of ordering cost and carrying cost at the EOQ?
options: Ordering cost is double the carrying cost
They are equal (both ₦1,008 in the Orange Nursery example)
questions.explanation: At the minimum of the total cost curve, the two curves cross.

questions.prompt: For the Suburban Fuel Oil Company (H = 4,000,000, S = ₦200, J = ₦0.04), what is the EOQ?
At a railway desk, λ = 20 per hour and the service time is 2 minutes per customer. What is the utilisation ρ?
For the same desk (λ = 20, μ = 30), what is the average number in the queue Lq?
For the same desk, what is the average time in the queue Wq?
questions.explanation: Wq = Lq / λ = 1.33 / 20 = 0.0667 hours = 4 minutes.

questions.prompt: For the same desk, what is the average time in the system W?
questions.explanation: W = 1 / (μ − λ) = 1 / 10 = 0.1 hours = 6 minutes.

questions.prompt: With λ = 25 per hour, μ = 10 per hour per server, s = 3 and Lq = 3.51, what is the average number in the system L?
For Orange Nursery (H = 144,000, S = ₦112, K = 0.18, P = ₦0.70), how many orders a year does the EOQ policy give?
How much does Orange Nursery save by moving from two orders of 72,000 a year (₦4,760) to the EOQ policy?
If Orange Nursery must also pay a storage surcharge W = ₦0.049 per unit a year, what happens to the EOQ?
options: It falls to 12,000 units, giving 12 orders a year
questions.explanation: Q* = √(2HS / (KP + 2W)) = √(32,256,000 / 0.224) = 12,000. Higher storage cost favours smaller, more frequent orders.
